source: data/postgame films (our squad ranked games, both teams), zero-API; meta shares from predgg-augments.json / predgg-builds.json (1.17.2)

method.score: Role-weighted mean of per-metric z-scores (capped ±3). Each metric is compared with the hero-role mean from the other films (leave-one-out), shrunk toward the role mean with k=10 games, divided by the role-wide spread. pred.gg performanceScore is 0 on every film row, so it is not used.
method.verdict: build = a loadout piece this player ran also scores higher on this hero-role in the OTHER films (this game left out; delta >= 0.4 and t >= 2, >=3 games each side) AND that trend spans >= 3 players with none over 60% of its games — otherwise it is one player's comfort setup and counts as player; and the public 1.17.2 win rate with vs without that piece (predgg-augments/builds, all ranked players) must not point the other way (trends[].public); team = teammates also scored >= 0.5 or the team won kills by 15+; matchup = pred.gg lane winrate >= 52.5% for their side (the engine matrix edge is listed as a factor only); player = none of those. Heuristic: a lead to check in the film, not proof.
method.caveats: Baselines come from our own films (182 games) across patches since April, against our squad's ranked bracket; most hero-roles have under 20 games. Treat trends with n < 5 as leads.
